account:
It is day 1, just after seven in the morning. I have read today's appointments and returned the books to the office chest. I am due in the office at eight, at the east-bank mill for a grain inspection at ten, home for lunch, back in the office for council letters at thirteen, at my neighbour's cottage for tea at fifteen, in the office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen.

The unusual business is the preparation of the town hall. Yesterday I saw builder put bread into the eastern table chest at (-50, -60, 30), then saw innkeeper deliver bread there as well. Lanterns have been placed in the hall. Secretary independently saw the lanterns and innkeeper's delivery and has been trying to find out the occasion. This morning I heard secretary calling to builder and innkeeper to ask what the bread and lanterns were for, but I have not heard an answer. The evening office note says the occasion and full arrangements remain unconfirmed.

Bread being gathered in a lit hall suggests a shared meal or gathering, perhaps an evening event, but that is only my inference. I do not know who is invited, when it is meant to happen, or why nobody has explained it to me. Neighbour previously identified builder as coordinating supplies and lighting, according to my office record, but did not confirm a particular occasion. Neighbour is now here at town hall early this morning; that may be ordinary business and is not proof of involvement. I want to ask directly without treating my suspicion that something is happening without me as an established fact.
